title: KCP model_complete request (DESIGN.md §14.1, §16.1-§16.3, §11.6.1 worker-operations family)
description: Mutation (meta required; §11.2: every state-changing operation requires meta). Worker-surface model call — `ctx.model.complete` on the wire. What is absent is the contract: no provider, host, URL, path, header, credential, or credential reference is expressible here, because agent code calls a logical model PROFILE and the broker resolves the destination from that profile's ModelProviderBinding (§16.3). The act_* / subject_digest / stable_execution_key members name byom's authorizing model_egress act; they are CLAIMS, re-derived by byomd inside execution_permit_consume, and the permit-channel token is byomd's own file keyed to that act — so naming another act's refs authorizes nothing. Registry (developer_assistant_v1): surface worker / invocation attempt only (assurance: workload identity plus invocation capability). Surface and actor kind are registry-enforced, not schema-expressible (gap note KG14).

fence_epoch.description: Every worker operation carries {attempt_id, fence_epoch}; an expired or superseded attempt receives stale-lease (§15.2).

model_profile_ref.description: The logical ModelProfile (§16.3). It selects an exact ModelProviderBinding revision and digest and cannot override its endpoint, account, region, transport, or provider terms.

purpose_ref.description: The stated purpose the DisclosureManifest binds (§16.2); authorization binds the final bytes for this purpose, not a broad topic name.

classification_ref.description: The classification of everything that leaves; the profile's allowed_classification_refs must permit it, re-checked immediately before use (§16.3).

prompt.description: The disclosed request text. Byte-capped so an over-cap prompt is refused before any manifest is built for it (§11.8).

system.description: The assistant/system instruction, recorded as its own ordered segment of the ProviderContextManifest chain (§16.3).

max_output_tokens.description: Must not exceed the profile's request_limits.output_tokens (§16.3).

stable_binding_key.description: The governed byom Episode binding this call runs inside. Both fences are re-presented to byomd; one current fence is not enough (family contract L21).

act_intent_ref.description: byom's authorized model_egress ActIntent, and the subject of the narrow permit channel byomd published for it (byom R34).

act_revision.description: The CAS revision execution_permit_consume expects on byom's act head.

subject_digest.description: byom's authorized act subject digest, echoed. Kovee canonicalizes its OWN effect separately (host_effect_digest); it never invents byom's subject.

context_manifest_ref.description: The HOST-owned ContextManifest the act's seats assented to, as byom committed it. execution_permit_consume presents this pair and byom compares BOTH members against its own committed act, so an act authorized under one context is not consumable under another (byom R3-A01). All-or-none with its digest.

context_manifest_digest.description: The exact content of that ContextManifest. Cross-boundary, so portable_public: byom holds the same bytes and compares them. It is also a member of the frozen kovee-host-effect-binding-v1 fragment byom rebuilds to re-derive host_effect_digest (R3-L01).

stable_execution_key.description: byom's kernel-derived one-shot key. It is the local Effect's identity (UNIQUE), and the ExecutionConsumptionReceipt must name exactly it or no byte leaves (§16.1 steps 1-4).

args.description: ctx.model.complete(profile, prompt, …) on the wire (§14.1); the SDK operation_key is sugar the supervisor combines with the invocation id into the durable deduplication key — carried as meta.idempotency_key.

commandMeta.description: Command.meta (§11.2). Required on every mutation; idempotency keys are scoped by authenticated actor, operation, and realm; expected_revision drives optimistic concurrency (mismatch is stale-revision).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (byom family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. Expressed as two CLOSED alternatives rather than one open object refined by a oneOf, so each arm states its own complete member set: an unkeyed public class with sha-256 and no key_ref, or a keyed erasure class with hmac-sha-256 and a mandatory key_ref. Substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.
digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash.

class.description: The unkeyed classes: recomputable by a counterparty, which is what makes cross-boundary agreement a machine check.
The keyed erasure classes: destroying the key erases exactly that object's (or that scope's) verifiability.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

ext.description: Extensions keyed by a reverse-domain namespace (§11.9); never interpreted as identity, authorization, budget, or policy.

identifier.description: Opaque identifier, at most 128 bytes (§11.8); visible-ASCII alphabet is a K0 extraction decision (spec/schemas/README.md).

protocolVersion.description: Negotiated KCP major.minor version; the initial protocol version is "0.1" (§11).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§11.8 rejects unsafe integers).

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context traceparent header value; excluded from the idempotency request digest (§11.2).
